name: Heirloom tomatoes
tile_uses: The tomato plate, toast, both jars, the weekend
why_now: July is peak tomato season in Southern California. Any ripe tomato — heirloom or not — is at its best right now. The heat concentrates sugars across every variety. Heirlooms are worth it if you see good ones, but a ripe vine tomato from Trader Joe's or Whole Foods will do the same work.
how_to_choose: Irregular shape is a good sign, not a flaw
Avoid anything refrigerated at the store
buy_this_much: 4–6 medium tomatoes for one person for the week
price_note: Vine and roma tomatoes are among the most affordable options year-round — and July is when they're actually worth buying. Heirlooms cost more but aren't required.

flavor_paths.name: Raw and salted
flavor_paths.description: Sliced thick, salted, left five minutes. The default.

flavor_paths.name: Charred
flavor_paths.description: Blistered in a dry pan for the salsa.

flavor_paths.name: In the jar
flavor_paths.description: Chopped into the vinaigrette with sherry vinegar.

weekday_uses: Sliced thick for the tomato plate
On tomato toast with an egg
weekend_use: Sliced thick beside slow-roasted salmon and burrata, with the vinaigrette spooned over.
storage: Counter only. Never refrigerate. Use within four or five days.
one_thing_to_learn: Smell the stem end before you buy. A tomato that smells like a tomato at the store will taste like one at home.
